name: Buggy Choke to North-South
summary: Moving to North-South after a Buggy Choke requires the top player to clear the bottom player's head-and-arm loop before establishing the next control.
description: Moving to North-South after a Buggy Choke requires the top player to clear the bottom player's head-and-arm loop before establishing the next control.
overview:
The top player is the choke defender even though this transition calls the moving player its attacker. Changing pins does not itself prove that the choke is gone. Clear the arm-and-leg loop first, and do not lift or slam the partner to escape.

Watch for an arm reaching past your head and connecting to the same-side leg. Avoid lifting, dropping, or twisting the partner's trapped leg to force an escape. Use safe inside frames before the arm-to-leg loop fully closes; do not pull or twist the partner's knee.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Kade and Tye Ruotolo — OG Buggy Choke](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zixbOyLpoOc); [Jay Rodriguez — three Buggy Choke mistakes](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MjKERx4N4mY).

flashcards.question: Buggy Choke to North-South (top): Which same-side connection must you clear?
flashcards.answer: Watch for an arm reaching past your head and connecting to the same-side leg.
flashcards.answer_line: Arm-leg loop on your head and arm

plausible: Arm circles head, no leg connection
Hand holds knee, your head outside
trap: Arm joins leg on your shoulder alone

flashcards.question: Buggy Choke to North-South (top): What should support your weight during early defense?
flashcards.answer: Keep supported weight on the mat; lifting or wrenching the connected leg is not a sound escape.
flashcards.answer_line: Knee or foot posts on the mat

plausible: Trapped shoulder, no knee posts
Your toes while lifting their hips
trap: Far hand alone, hips over their head

flashcards.question: Buggy Choke to North-South (top): When is an inside frame useful against the connection?
flashcards.answer: Use safe inside frames before the arm-to-leg loop fully closes; do not pull or twist the partner's knee.
flashcards.answer_line: Before hand and leg close the loop

plausible: After neck tightens, before circling
After one step with the loop closed
trap: Once grip locks, elbow meets knee

flashcards.question: Buggy Choke to North-South (top): Which clearance must precede the circle to north-south?
flashcards.answer: Move only through available space after the loop opens; tap if the neck is already enclosed.
flashcards.answer_line: Head and arm released from the loop

plausible: Just near knee beyond their hip
Chin tucked, loop remaining shut
trap: One hand free, neck still enclosed

flashcards.answer_line: Block hips, circle outside the legs

plausible: Chase head, leave their hips mobile

defender.name: Buggy Choke to North-South Defender
defender.description: Buggy Choke to North-South (defender): Use safe shoulder and hip frames to turn partly onto the side before reaching for the leg. Check that the loop contains the necessary upper-body configuration rather than merely hugging your leg.
defender.overview:
The top player is the choke defender even though this transition calls the moving player its attacker. Changing pins does not itself prove that the choke is gone. Clear the arm-and-leg loop first, and do not lift or slam the partner to escape.

Use safe shoulder and hip frames to turn partly onto the side before reaching for the leg. Check that the loop contains the necessary upper-body configuration rather than merely hugging your leg. Shorten the connection through body position, not by pulling the foot hard toward the face.

Close space with the arm, leg, and torso while avoiding twisting force on your own knee. Use a disengaging opponent's movement to insert frames and knees if the choke is lost. Let go when the partner begins lifting you from the mat; do not hang from the choke or invite a slam.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

The Buggy holder shortens the loop with shoulder pressure toward the hip, not by wrenching the foot. If the loop is lost, stop chasing it and make a framed hip escape while the opponent circles, keeping the knees available to return inside.
key_principles: Build the angle: Use safe shoulder and hip frames to turn partly onto the side before reaching for the leg.
Enclose head and arm: Check that the loop contains the necessary upper-body configuration rather than merely hugging your leg.
Keep elbow near knee: Shorten the connection through body position, not by pulling the foot hard toward the face.
Use the torso connection: Close space with the arm, leg, and torso while avoiding twisting force on your own knee.
Recover guard when space opens: Use a disengaging opponent's movement to insert frames and knees if the choke is lost.
Release if lifted: Let go when the partner begins lifting you from the mat; do not hang from the choke or invite a slam.

flashcards.question: Buggy Choke to North-South (bottom): What body position reduces your reach to the linking leg?
flashcards.answer: Use safe shoulder and hip frames to turn partly onto the side before reaching for the leg.

plausible: Flat back with the elbow extended
Side angle, raised knee drifts away
trap: Flat back, hips extend from shoulder

flashcards.question: Buggy Choke to North-South (bottom): What must your same-side arm-leg loop enclose?
flashcards.answer: The Buggy loop encloses the top player's head and one arm; a grip on the leg alone does not suffice.
flashcards.answer_line: Their head and one arm together

plausible: Their head only, both arms outside
Their arm only, head left outside
trap: Only your leg, head past your elbow

flashcards.question: Buggy Choke to North-South (bottom): With the elbow near the knee, what replaces pulling the foot?
flashcards.answer: Close the enclosure through torso position, keeping the elbow near the knee instead of levering the foot.

plausible: Move shoulder away, pull toes inward
Extend torso to lengthen the reach
trap: Raise elbow away, keep torso flat

flashcards.question: Buggy Choke to North-South (bottom): The loop is lost as they circle. How do you recover space?
flashcards.answer: Once the loop fails, abandon it and use a framed hip escape while knee space remains available.
flashcards.answer_line: Frame, move hips, bring knees inside

plausible: Chase old foot grip with both arms
Turn the knees away from their path
trap: Push on straight arms, hips still
